zh: 所以我一直在思考，如何把我的内容流程重塑为 AI 原生或 AI 辅助的？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我基本上会得到 15 个内容峰值。

speaker: Unknown
en: How you get it to not write slop.
zh: 你怎么让它不写出垃圾内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only time in my view that the content machine actually produces slop is more of an indictment of the person not sharing good enough ideas during the interview step than the AI writing bad stuff.
zh: 在我看来，内容机器真正产出垃圾内容的唯一情况，更多是在面试步骤中那个人没有分享足够好的创意的问题，而不是 AI 写出了糟糕的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what you're saying is we are actually the slop.
zh: 所以你的意思是，我们其实才是垃圾内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: My take is that AI slop is hilariously people just pointing the finger at themselves and saying, I'm not intelligent enough.
zh: 我的看法是，AI 垃圾内容这事儿可笑之处在于，人们其实只是在指着自己说，我不够聪明。

en: Alex, I am excited about this episode because I tell everybody in order to make it, certainly as a bootstrapped entrepreneur, you have to do one thing and it's not vibe code.
zh: Alex，我对这一集很兴奋，因为我告诉所有人，要想成功，当然作为一名自筹资金的创业者，你必须做一件事，而且这不是 vibe coding。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is climb cringe mountain.
zh: 而是攀登“尴尬山”。

en: You have to post.
zh: 你必须发帖。

zh: 而我要说，作为一个真正的工程师中的工程师，我为了避开谈论自己的业务，字面意义上什么都能造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are surprised about this.
zh: 人们对这一点感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: So please tell me, how have you started to use AI?
zh: 所以请告诉我，你是怎么开始使用 AI 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you start to use AI to build the content engine at your company?
zh: 你为什么开始用 AI 来打造你公司的内容引擎？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, first of all, thanks so much for having me.
zh: 嗯，首先，非常感谢你邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I, first of all, I totally ascribe to climbing AI Cringe Mountain.
zh: 所以我，首先，我完全认同攀登 AI“尴尬山”这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I probably move on like the totally opposite side of the spectrum, which is like I am happy to be cringy and just like shoot as many shots on goal to to sell kind of what I'm doing, because my belief is people who believe that like if you build it, they will come.
zh: 我可能处在完全相反的另一个极端，就是我很乐意表现得尴尬，就是尽情地多次射门去推销我正在做的事情，因为我的信念是，那些相信“如果你把它造出来，人们自然就会来”的人——

speaker: Unknown
en: I just.
zh: 我只是。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a world in which distribution is more important than ever before, I don't think that's necessarily the case or isn't most of the time.
zh: 在一个分发比以往任何时候都更重要的世界里，我不认为情况一定是那样，或者说大多数时候不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically there have been two problems within the context of 10X that I've been trying to solve.
zh: 所以基本上，在 10X 的背景下，有两个我一直试图解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just for folks that don't know what 10X is, applied AI company helping mid-market and enterprise companies go through their AI transformation.
zh: 给那些不知道 10X 是什么的人说明一下，它是一家应用 AI 公司，帮助中型市场和企业级公司完成他们的 AI 转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we do everything from strategy to forward deployed engineering.
zh: 我们做的事情从战略到前置部署工程都有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first is...
zh: 所以第一个是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I have been creating content on the internet for the last 10 years, basically since I started Morning Brew when I was in college.
zh: 过去 10 年我一直在互联网上创作内容，基本上从我大学时创办 Morning Brew 就开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think creating content has afforded me so many opportunities, but I am capped on the amount of time that I can spend creating content every day.
zh: 我认为创作内容给了我很多机会，但我每天能花在创作内容上的时间是有限的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I would say 25% of my time can be spent creating content.
zh: 比如我会说我 25% 的时间可以用来创作内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I've been basically thinking about
zh: 所以我基本上一直在思考

speaker: Unknown
en: How can I maximize the value of that 25% of my time?
zh: 我如何才能最大化这 25% 时间中的价值?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I've thought a lot about is how can I re-engineer my content process to be AI native or AI assisted while making sure that I'm not putting out AI slop?
zh: 我反复思考的一个问题是，我如何能重新设计我的内容流程，使其成为 AI 原生或 AI 辅助的，同时确保我不会发布 AI 垃圾内容?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think that's what creates so much aversion to AI for people, especially around creating content, is that it's just going to spit out kind of just...
zh: 因为我认为这正是人们对 AI 产生如此多抵触情绪的原因，尤其是在内容创作方面，就是它只会吐出那种……

speaker: Unknown
en: Really mid stuff that sounds like everything else that's been said on the Internet.
zh: 真的很平庸的东西，听起来和互联网上说过的其他所有东西都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is, you know, every business I build, whether it's a media company or non media company, I think we need to think more about building media companies on top of our businesses in the future.
zh: 第二个是，你知道，我建立的每一个企业，无论是媒体公司还是非媒体公司，我认为我们未来需要更多地思考在我们的业务之上构建媒体公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for that is in a post AI world where technology gets more commoditized than ever before, there are fewer moats in business.
zh: 原因在于，在一个 AI 后世界，技术比以往任何时候都更加商品化，商业中的护城河更少了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I believe that trusted distribution is one of them.
zh: 而我相信可信的分发渠道就是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So overall, I am building a media company on top of 10X, and I think that, you know, I'm gonna do all the obvious things, like bring full-time creators onto staff, writers, we're gonna have a newsletter, all these things, but I don't think enough companies think about turning their own employees into creators if they want to do that.
zh: 所以总的来说，我正在 10X 之上构建一家媒体公司，我认为，你知道，我会做所有显而易见的事情，比如把全职创作者招进团队、写作者，我们会有一个 newsletter,所有这些事情，但我认为没有足够的公司去思考如何把自己的员工变成创作者——如果他们想这么做的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the other problem I've been trying to solve is how do I make it as easy as humanly possible for employees to be creators while they have full-time jobs?
zh: 所以我一直在试图解决的另一个问题是，如何让员工在有全职工作的情况下，能尽可能轻松地成为创作者?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was kind of the genesis of this content machine idea was optimizing for these two problems.
zh: 所以这就是这个内容机器想法的起源，就是针对这两个问题进行优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this because, one, I went through this myself.
zh: 我很喜欢这个，因为，第一，我自己经历过这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I am a at chief product officer on TikTok.
zh: 你知道，我是 TikTok 的首席产品官。

speaker: Unknown
en: I went through this phase where I was like, you know what?
zh: 我经历过这样一个阶段，我当时想，你知道吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of my job as an executive when I had those jobs was to be the marketing face of the company.
zh: 当我担任那些职位时，作为高管，我工作的一部分就是成为公司的市场形象代言人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, I used to say in SaaS, you weren't buying the product, you were buying the roadmap.
zh: 而且，你知道，我过去在 SaaS 领域常说，你买的不是产品，你买的是路线图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I would tell my team is they're not buying the roadmap, they're buying the team.
zh: 而我会告诉我团队的是，他们买的不是路线图，他们买的是团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is like they believe this team can execute on the vision.
zh: 这就像是，他们相信这个团队能够执行这个愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they want to bet with either a subscription or an engagement or whatever on the team.
zh: 所以他们想要用订阅或合作或任何方式来押注这个团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I talked to a lot of CEOs right now that are really unsettled by the current state of marketing where existing channels have diminishing returns.
zh: 我现在和很多 CEO 交流过，他们对当前营销的现状感到非常不安，因为现有渠道的回报在递减。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not seeing the old stuff really work.
zh: 他们发现老办法真的不管用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every single one of them I tell your number one marketing channel should be your employees.
zh: 我对他们每一个人都说，你的第一营销渠道应该是你的员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I love that you're investing in this.
zh: 所以我很高兴你在这方面进行投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, my big concern is, and I have a little bit of a, you know, content distribution engine going as well with some AI in it, is AI is just out of the box pretty terrible at writing compelling copy.
zh: 现在，我最大的顾虑是——我自己也有一个带一些 AI 的、你知道的，内容分发引擎在运转——AI 开箱即用地写不出有吸引力的文案，真的相当糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we've all seen this.
zh: 我想我们所有人都见过这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're all really critical of it, but it seems like you figured this out.
zh: 我们都对它非常挑剔，但看起来你已经解决了这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd love to hear just a little bit of your process, where you think AI fits, where it doesn't, how you get it to not write slop.
zh: 所以我很想听你讲讲你的流程，你认为 AI 适合哪些环节、不适合哪些环节，你如何让它不写垃圾内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, totally.
zh: 是的，完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have a few thoughts here.
zh: 我这里有几个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were talking about this before, which is Lulu Miservi has talked about this idea of it's a shame when the best writers in the world use AI because they cap their ceiling.
zh: 我们之前聊过这个，就是 Lulu Miservi 谈过这样一个观点：如果世界上最好的写作者使用 AI,那是一种遗憾，因为他们给自己封了顶。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so her view is AI will raise the floor of bad writers, but then cap the ceiling of great writers.
zh: 所以她的观点是，AI 会提高糟糕写作者的下限，但会封住优秀写作者的上限。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I agree with that with nuance.
zh: 我认为我在细微处同意这个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing I'll say is that
zh: 我首先要说的是

speaker: Unknown
en: Writing and creating content is a multi-step process, which we'll go through.
zh: 写作和创作内容是一个多步骤的流程，我们会过一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think just saying that using AI in any part of the content process is going to lower your ceiling is not necessarily true.
zh: 而且我认为，仅仅说在内容流程的任何环节使用 AI 都会降低你的上限，这不一定正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if we were to say for the actual drafting or editing part of the content process, using AI lowers your ceiling, I can buy that and I can understand if you are a gifted writers in the top 1% of writers, how basically just
zh: 我想，如果我们说在内容流程中实际起草或编辑的部分，使用 AI 会降低你的上限，这个我可以接受，我也可以理解，如果你是一位有天赋的、处于写作者前 1% 的人，基本上只是

speaker: Unknown
en: Banking on a model that's been trained on the entire corpus of the internet and so by definition will be average versus you being a above average or an acceptable writer.
zh: 押注在一个在整个互联网语料库上训练过的模型上，而这个模型按定义来说就是平均水平的， versus 你是一个高于平均水平或合格水平的写作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would be worse?
zh: 为什么会更糟呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally get that.
zh: 完全理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are many parts of a content process and I think some of these parts you can use AI and still continue to actually raise your ceiling, not lower it.
zh: 但内容流程有很多环节，我认为其中一些环节你可以使用 AI,同时实际上继续提高你的上限，而不是降低它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other piece of it is...
zh: 另一方面是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I always think about alternatives.
zh: 我总是会考虑替代方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the alternative for our team at 10X, and we can talk a little bit in a bit about how we're incentivizing people to create, but the alternative before this content machine was people just not creating content.
zh: 所以对我们在 10X 的团队来说——我们稍后可以聊聊我们如何激励人们去创作——在这台内容机器之前的替代方案，就是人们干脆不创作内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's like, if I have two options, get people to create content around their expertise and the things that they're doing in work or not create, of course I'm going to take the first every single day of the week.
zh: 所以就是说，如果我有两个选项：让人们围绕他们的专业知识和他们在工作中做的事情创作内容，或者不创作，当然我会每个星期每一天都选第一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what I can do is kind of take you through how I thought about my content process and then how I transformed it.
zh: 所以我能做的，就是带你过一遍我是如何思考我的内容流程的，然后我是如何改造它的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even though we're talking about it in the context of using AI for content, our view at 10X and my view is like you kind of use this kind of process mapping and then rebuilding for any process in your work.
zh: 即使我们是在使用 AI 做内容的语境下谈论它，我们在 10X 的观点和我个人的观点是，你其实可以把这种流程映射和重建的方法用在工作中任何流程上。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is just kind of the world that I know.
zh: 这只是我所熟悉的领域而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so this is when I started this process, I basically just drew out exactly how the content process works today.
zh: 好的,这就是我开始这个过程的时候,我基本上就是把如今的内容流程是如何运作的完整画了出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for anyone creating content, you basically start by finding inspiration.
zh: 所以对于任何创作内容的人来说,你基本上都是从寻找灵感开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And historically speaking, the hardest thing for not even just people who are trying to create content for the first time, but like anyone, I would actually say, especially people who are creators is...
zh: 从历史上讲,最难的不仅仅是那些第一次尝试创作内容的人,而是所有人,我甚至会说,尤其是创作者,那就是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Finding new ideas that feel novel and interesting and just don't feel like tired regurgitation of what's been said is really hard.
zh: 找到让人觉得新颖有趣的想法,而不是那种把已经说过的话老调重弹,这真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first step is finding an idea.
zh: 所以第一步是找到一个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second step or like 1B is if it is an idea related to a lived experience where you feel fully informed about the idea, then you can skip the research step.
zh: 第二步,或者说是 1B,如果这是一个与你亲身经历相关的想法,你对这个想法完全了解,那么你可以跳过研究这一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for a lot of ideas, you'll actually have to research.
zh: 但对于很多想法来说,你实际上必须做研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then the next step is you're going to get all of your thoughts out on paper where it's kind of like the
zh: 接下来的步骤是你要把所有的想法都写在纸上,这有点像是

speaker: Unknown
en: The the mental vomiting of your thoughts around the idea.
zh: 把你围绕这个想法的思绪来一场精神上的呕吐。

speaker: Unknown
en: Next step is you decide what is kind of the anchor format that you want to create a piece of content around, whether it's long form website, LinkedIn, newsletter, etc.
zh: 下一步是你决定想要围绕什么锚定格式来创作一篇内容,无论是长篇网站文章、LinkedIn、newsletter 等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you write the piece, then you review a draft, you revise it.
zh: 然后你写这篇内容,然后审阅草稿,进行修改。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you go through the editing process, you publish it and then.
zh: 所以你要经历编辑流程,然后发布它,接着。
